extracted.intended_audience: CIHR/tri-agency applicants, peer reviewers, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and conducting responsible research assessment in CIHR grant programs and peer review, emphasizing holistic evaluation of contributions, reducing bias, and alignment with DORA and tri-agency policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value a range of research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize and value a range of research contributions that can lead to impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application processes should encourage the inclusion of a broad range of contributions, from publications to societal outputs, in the Most Significant Contributions section. Consider datasets, software, and other outputs in addition to publications; use the Tri-Agency narrative CV to demonstrate a research narrative, career trajectories, and mentorship roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics as surrogates (DORA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors, as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist's contributions, or in hiring, promotion, or funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid relying on Journal Impact Factor or similar metrics when evaluating individual outputs; consider alternative indicators and qualitative evidence of value and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on scientific content rather than publication metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For funding agencies: be explicit about the criteria used in evaluating scientific productivity and clearly highlight that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make evaluation criteria transparent, and especially for early-stage investigators emphasize content and contribution over where an article was published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider the value and impact of all research outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of research assessment, consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a broad range of impact measures, including qualitative indicators such as influence on policy and practice, when assessing outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider applicant context and career circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the applicant's context (e.g., career stage, leave history) when assessing their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid penalizing non-linear careers or leave periods; take career stage and circumstances into account when judging productivity and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage inclusion of career narrative and mentorship roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Application processes should encourage detailed descriptions of career trajectories and mentorship roles (e.g., via the Tri-Agency narrative CV).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow applicants to describe career narratives and mentorship contributions to give a fuller picture of their research role and impact beyond publication lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review should assess diverse contributions and emphasize quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review guidelines ask reviewers to consider a greater variety of contributions, avoid relying on quantitative indicators, focus on quality over quantity, and consider the applicant's context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should broaden the scope of what counts as contribution (societal impacts, datasets, software), prioritize quality, and use applicant context to interpret productivity rather than raw counts or metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical training and supports to reduce bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide training and supports for applicants and peer reviewers to reduce bias and support a fair process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tri-agency Excellence in Peer and Merit Review learning modules (Module 1: Biases in the Research Ecosystem; Module 2: Mitigating Bias in the Peer and Merit Review Processes) are mandatory for all CIHR reviewers; include DORA content to discourage inappropriate metric use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit and transparent about evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding bodies should be explicit about the criteria used to evaluate scientific productivity of grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly communicate expectations to applicants and reviewers, especially regarding how non-traditional outputs and qualitative impacts will be weighed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple metrics and qualitative evidence when documenting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of article metrics and indicators on personal/supporting statements as evidence of the impact of individual published articles and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine quantitative indicators with qualitative descriptions of influence (e.g., policy change, practice uptake) rather than relying on single metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researchers should assess based on content and cite appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: When involved in committees making decisions about funding, hiring, tenure, or promotion, make assessments based on scientific content rather than publication metrics; cite primary literature whenever appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give credit to primary sources rather than reviews to ensure proper attribution; actively challenge assessment practices that rely inappropriately on Journal Impact Factors and teach best practices that focus on specific outputs' value and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align assessment practices with DORA and international initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR is a signatory to DORA and commits to improving research evaluation beyond widely used journal-based metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt DORA recommendations (e.g., avoid journal-based metrics, consider diverse outputs and impacts) and engage with Research on Research initiatives (RoRI) to gather evidence and experiment with better evaluation tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue research excellence that is inclusive, transparent, and impact-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: CIHR's Research Excellence Framework positions research assessment to be inclusive, collaborative, transparent, culturally safe, and focused on real-world impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design assessment processes that support inclusion, cultural safety, collaboration, transparency, and demonstrable societal or policy impact as dimensions of research excellence.
